question: Mihira Bhoja, a famous ruler of the Pratiharas, adopted which title?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Adivaraha**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Mihira Bhoja, one of the most notable rulers of the Pratihara dynasty, adopted the title **Adivaraha**, which symbolized his association with Lord Vishnu's Varaha (boar) incarnation.
 
• The title "Adivaraha" reflects the ruler's dedication to Vaishnavism, which was a significant aspect of his reign.
 
• Mihira Bhoja was known for strengthening the Pratihara dynasty's power and expanding its territorial reach during the 9th century CE.
 
• His reign is marked by significant advancements in administration, military organization, and cultural development under the Pratiharas.
 
• The use of the title "Adivaraha" was also an assertion of divine legitimacy and authority over his kingdom.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Pratihara Dynasty:**

 
 
• The Gurjara-Pratihara dynasty was one of the three main powers of early medieval India, alongside the Palas and Rashtrakutas.
 
• Their empire extended over northern and western India, and they were known for their resistance to Arab invasions.
 
 
 
• **Vaishnavism:**
 
 
• A major tradition within Hinduism that worships Vishnu and his avatars, such as Rama and Krishna, as the supreme deities.
 
• It played a significant role in shaping the religious and cultural practices of medieval India.
 
 
 
• **Varaha Avatar:**
 
 
• Varaha is the third avatar of Vishnu, depicted as a boar that rescued the Earth (personified as the goddess Bhudevi) from the demon Hiranyaksha.
 
• This avatar signifies the triumph of good over evil and the restoration of cosmic order (dharma).
 
 
 
• **Mihira Bhoja's Legacy:**
 
 
• He is celebrated for his military conquests and efficient administration.
 
• His empire acted as a crucial cultural and political bridge between different regions of India during his rule.
